claims.claim: **Chest infection is the commonest reason children with CP are admitted.** They can deteriorate quickly and may need higher levels of support.
claims.source_text: Chest infections are the most common reason for children with cerebral palsy to require hospital admission … Children with cerebral palsy can deteriorate quickly and may require higher levels of supportive care
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Organisms are the same as in other children; consider anaerobes if aspiration contributes.**
claims.source_text: Causative organisms are the same as for other children Consider anaerobic organisms if aspiration is a contributing factor
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Predisposing factors** include aspiration from pseudobulbar palsy, increased secretions, poor cough, reflux, severe scoliosis, malnutrition, and reduced airway protection from fluctuating consciousness (eg benzodiazepines).
claims.source_text: pseudobulbar palsy leading to aspiration of saliva, food or fluid increased secretions poor cough gastro-oesophageal reflux decreased mobility severe scoliosis malnutrition … impaired airway protection secondary to fluctuations in level of consciousness, which may be due to medications eg benzodiazepines
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ask specifically about:** fever or hypothermia · apnoea · vomiting or feed intolerance · aspiration risk · change in baseline consciousness · increased oxygen or suction needs.
claims.source_text: Fever or hypothermia Apnoea Vomiting/unable to tolerate usual feeding regimen Risk of aspiration Change in baseline level of consciousness Increased oxygen or suction requirements
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Risk factors for severe illness:** previous ICU admission for pneumonia · pre-existing respiratory failure · home non-invasive support · scoliosis · more seizures in a known seizure disorder.
claims.source_text: Risk factors for severe respiratory illness Previous ICU admission for pneumonia Pre-existing respiratory failure Home respiratory non-invasive support Scoliosis Increased seizure activity if known seizure disorder
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Work of breathing can be exacerbated by dystonia**; look for upper airway obstruction.
claims.source_text: Signs of upper airway obstruction Increased work of breathing, can be exacerbated by dystonia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider severe pneumonia with rapid deterioration or any of:** severe respiratory distress · marked tachycardia · severe hypoxaemia or cyanosis · reduced consciousness from baseline · increasing respiratory support.
claims.source_text: Severe pneumonia should be considered if there is a rapid deterioration and/or any of the following are present: severe respiratory distress marked tachycardia severe hypoxaemia or cyanosis decreased level of consciousness/deterioration in baseline level of consciousness increased respiratory supports required
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Follow the pneumonia guideline, with a lower threshold for antibiotics in severe CP and a lower threshold for admission.**
claims.source_text: Investigations and treatment of pneumonia in children with cerebral palsy should follow the pneumonia guideline … Have a lower threshold for starting antibiotics in children with severe cerebral palsy Have a lower threshold for admission
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chest X-rays are hard to read with scoliosis** — compare with previous films.
claims.source_text: Chest X-rays may be difficult to interpret in children with scoliosis. It can be helpful to compare with previous X-rays
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Tell a senior clinician and/or ICU early for:** acute respiratory failure · severe distress · **FiO2 >50% (>6 L/min)** or more than baseline non-invasive support · an unwell child with severe-illness risk factors.
claims.source_text: Inform senior clinician and/or ICU early if: Acute respiratory failure Severe respiratory distress Oxygen requirement FiO2 >50% (>6L/min) or requiring increase in baseline non-invasive support Unwell and has risk factors for severe illness (as above)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Penicillin gives adequate anaerobic cover for aspiration.** Consider **oseltamivir** for influenza.
claims.source_text: Penicillin provides adequate anaerobic cover for aspiration in children … Consider Oseltamivir to cover influenza virus
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Positioning:** with significant scoliosis, sit the child up with the better-inflated lung up. Consider a **nasopharyngeal airway** in severe CP with upper airway obstruction, especially if drowsy and hypoxic.
claims.source_text: If significant scoliosis, position the child sitting up, with the ‘better inflated lung’ up … Consider nasopharyngeal airways in severe cerebral palsy and upper airway obstruction (especially if drowsy/decreased consciousness and hypoxic)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give oxygen if SpO2 is below 90% in room air**, humidified if possible.
claims.source_text: Give oxygen if oxygen saturations are <90% in room air If possible, administer humidified oxygen
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Trial salbutamol if there is bronchospasm** (wheeze, hyperinflation) and reassess.
claims.source_text: Consider trial of Salbutamol if evidence of bronchospasm (wheeze, hyperinflation) and reassess for improvement
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Secretions:** nebulised saline **5 mL of sodium chloride 0.9%** may help; oropharyngeal suction if the child cannot clear secretions; chest physiotherapy for large-airway secretions with a poor cough, or focal consolidation.
claims.source_text: Nebulised saline (5mls of sodium chloride 0.9%) may help mobilise secretions … Oro-pharyngeal suction may be useful if the child is unable to clear oral secretions … Chest physiotherapy is helpful if children have large airway secretions and a poor cough, or focal consolidation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Anticholinergics such as glycopyrrolate thicken secretions** and may need reducing during acute illness — discuss with a senior.
claims.source_text: Be aware of anticholinergics eg glycopyrrolate which thicken secretions. These may need to be reduced during acute illness. Discuss with a senior clinician
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Withhold feeds with moderate or severe work of breathing; give enteral or IV fluids at two-thirds maintenance** unless dehydrated.
claims.source_text: Withhold feeds if moderate or severe work of breathing and give enteral/IV fluids at two-thirds maintenance rate unless dehydrated
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider transfer for** severe or complicated pneumonia, **FiO2 >50% (>6 L/min)**, or care beyond the local hospital.
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when Severe or complicated pneumonia FiO2 requirement >50% (>6L/min) Requiring care above the level of comfort of the local hospital
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** oxygenation and oral intake/feeds are adequate and enteral antibiotics, if needed, are tolerated.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Child is maintaining adequate oxygenation and oral intake/feeds and tolerating enteral antibiotics if required
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severe CP: annual influenza vaccine** on top of the schedule; consider further pneumococcal vaccination.
claims.source_text: Children with severe cerebral palsy should receive the annual influenza vaccine in addition to the usual vaccines on the schedule … Consider indications and eligibility for further pneumococcal vaccination
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23
